description: This inventory lists 623 closed and abandoned landfills in the 16-county North Central Texas region around Dallas and Fort Worth, maintained by the North Central Texas Council of Governments. It began from a study by Southwest Texas State University for the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality; 136 of the sites were permitted by the state and 487 were unauthorised and are now considered abandoned. In the early 2000s the council researched each site further and, where possible, added location, current land use, ownership and boundaries from county deed records. Coverage is the 16 counties of the region. The inventory is free and available on the council website as a county-by-county list and a searchable map, and the database can be browsed with an online form. No licence is stated. Caveats: the council notes that the information is historic, comes from varied sources, is sometimes incomplete and should not be taken as definitive evidence of the presence or absence of a landfill. Simulation uses: screening legacy landfills against flood, subsidence and development plans, and adding them to condition and contamination risk studies for the region's infrastructure. Related records: the TCEQ statewide inventory (data-tceq-closed-msw-landfill-inventory) is the parent list.
